    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a discussion on CNBC's Halftime Report Wednesday, the question came up: Why can't Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh hold the line on interest rates the way his icon Alan Greenspan did at the beginning of the dot-com era?
    • Greenspan famously leaned against inflation hawks on his committee in 1995 and 1996, holding the line on interest rates amid strong growth, because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet revolution.
    • It would be nice if Warsh could follow the same playbook amid the artificial intelligence build-out and keep rates steady until the productivity arrives.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a discussion on CNBC's Halftime Report Wednesday, the question came up: Why can't Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh hold the line on interest rates the way his icon Alan Greenspan did at the beginning of the dot-com era?

    Greenspan famously leaned against inflation hawks on his committee in 1995 and 1996, holding the line on interest rates amid strong growth, because he believed in the productivity promise of the internet revolution.

    It would be nice if Warsh could follow the same playbook amid the artificial intelligence build-out and keep rates steady until the productivity arrives. Unfortunately, a quick look at the numbers shows just how different the situation is for Warsh when it comes to inflation, the magnitude of the capital-investment boom and the monetary and fiscal stimulus boosting the economy.

    Bottom line: the Fed looks like it has to hike — and maybe substantially — to be anywhere close to the position where the Fed was in Greenspan's time at the dawn of a major technological revolution.

    In a recent development, it may be that the massive capex spending on AI will mean more productivity and less inflation down the road. But the front-end build-out is proving to be more inflationary, and more challenging, to a Fed already dealing with high inflation. In many ways, that's the opposite of what Greenspan had to handle.

    Investors often favor dividend stocks for their regular income and the promise of potential share price appreciation. But selecting the right dividend stocks from a huge pool of companies can be difficult.

    Top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend-paying stocks, as their recommendations are backed by thorough analysis of a company's financials.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that devon Energy (DVN), an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production tech giant, reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. The company confirmed a quarterly dividend of 32 cents per share for the fourth quarter, payable December 30. Based on the fixed dividends paid over the trailing 12 months, DVN yields 2.85%.

    After hosting a virtual investor meeting with management, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Devon, with a price target of $59. Mehta mentioned that he is now more confident in management's outlook for delivering strong near-term capital returns as well as efforts to drive operational efficiencies and productivity gains.

    Sources indicate that devon sees an opportunity to increase share repurchases, driven by solid free cash flow (FCF), contributions from the Eagle Ford divestiture and continued improvement in the balance sheet, Mehta mentioned. Devon expects share buybacks worth more than $1 billion in Q4 2026, up from $414 million in the third quarter, backed by a strong pricing backdrop and improved capital efficiency.

    Sources indicate that mehta, a 5-star analyst, said Devon expects about $6.3 billion of excess FCF in 2027, including about $3.5 billion of net proceeds from the Eagle Ford sale. That would enable the organization to accelerate buybacks while progressing toward its goal of reducing gross debt to about $9 billion by early 2027. Mehta noted that under DVN's framework to return up to 70% of annual FCF, management favors share buybacks as it believes the stock is discounted compared to large-cap peers.

    "Management expects continued capital efficiency gains from merger synergies, extended laterals, surfactant adoption and development of the newly acquired federal acreage," Mehta noted.

    Industry observers note that mehta ranks No. 876 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.1%. See Devon Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Energy Transfer (ET), is a limited partnership that operates about 140,000 miles of pipeline and associated energy infrastructure. The company recently confirmed third-quarter results showing net income per common unit growing about 18% year-over-year, to 33 cents. ET's cash distribution for Q3 2026 was 34.25 cents per common unit, up more than 3% year-over-year. At an annualized distribution of $1.37 per share, Energy Transfer yields more than 7%.

    It has been revealed that TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer with a price target of $25. The company delivered better-than-expected Q3 results and confirmed the 1.2 billion cubic feet per day (bcf/d) South Mississippi Pipeline, a 215-mile, 36-inch natural gas line linking the Perryville Hub to the Florida Gas Transmission (FGT) network, Gabelman said.     • In a recent development, spaceX shares rose 4.83% in Friday's shortened trading session, amid broader Nasdaq gains and after CEO Elon Musk expanded his SpaceX share-donation blueprint for U.S.
    • Other tech-related stocks, including Micron, Qualcomm, Lumentum and Tesla all gained over 5% on Friday as the sector rebounded from a heavy sell-off earlier this week.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, spaceX shares rose 4.83% in Friday's shortened trading session, amid broader Nasdaq gains and after CEO Elon Musk expanded his SpaceX share-donation blueprint for U.S. children.

    Other tech-related stocks, including Micron, Qualcomm, Lumentum and Tesla all gained over 5% on Friday as the sector rebounded from a heavy sell-off earlier this week. SanDisk was Friday's biggest mover as investors rotated back into some AI trade names, surging 15.96%.

    Musk posted on X on Thursday, "I will be donating another share of SpaceX to all kids in America every year.".

    According to recent reports, after Musk's post, SpaceX shares jumped more than 7% in overnight trading on Blue Ocean ATS, an alternative trading system for U.S. equities that runs during the nighttime hours. U.S. stock exchanges were closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and closed at 1 p.m. ET on Friday.

    Shares closed 1.30% higher on Wednesday ahead of Thanksgiving.

    The latest pledge follows SpaceX's announcement Wednesday that it would donate one share of its Class A stock to all active Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children, with Musk personally matching the gift.

    In a separate post on X, Musk said SpaceX's contribution would be transferred next month, while his personal donation would follow when his lockup period expires in June next year.

    Nearly 70 million Trump Accounts had been created as of October, according to the White House.

    Since the program's launch in July, families and friends have contributed more than $1 billion to the accounts, bringing total deposits from all sources to more than $9 billion, CNBC reported earlier this week.

    The FCC also revealed Wednesday that it granted SpaceX approval to deploy 1 million data center satellites for the tech giant's Starmind constellation.

    Speaking on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Friday, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said the authorization of SpaceX's satellites will have ripple effects within the industry as well.

    "Not just SpaceX, but all sorts of different players in this market. Because at the end of the day, we want everyone to compete and succeed. I think we're going to see a lot of players entering this space soon," Carr said.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Budget airline Norse Atlantic files for bankruptcy in Europe after failing to secure funding

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (411 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Budget carrier Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy Friday, saying it failed to secure funding after soaring fuel costs strained the manufacturer's operations throughout the year.
    • Its parent manufacturer, Norse Atlantic ASA, concluded that the Norwegian carrier no longer has a basis to continue operations.
    • "Despite extensive efforts, the Organization has so far not been able to secure sufficient funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs," the firm noted in a statement Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Budget carrier Norse Atlantic filed for bankruptcy Friday, saying it failed to secure funding after soaring fuel costs strained the manufacturer's operations throughout the year.

    Its parent manufacturer, Norse Atlantic ASA, concluded that the Norwegian carrier no longer has a basis to continue operations.

    "Despite extensive efforts, the Organization has so far not been able to secure sufficient funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs," the firm noted in a statement Friday.

    According to recent reports, it comes days after Norse remarked it's facing a "critical financial situation" and was considering its options from a strategic takeover to ACMI contracts, which refer to short-term capacity leasing. The company's shares closed 85% lower on Wednesday.

    The board has now filed a bankruptcy petition with the Agder District Court, where a trustee will be appointed to manage the process further.

    "The Board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has made the difficult decision to file for bankruptcy despite extensive efforts from the Firm and the Group to find a solution," Norse Atlantic CEO Eivind Roald mentioned.

    According to recent reports, "We are deeply sorry for the impact this has on our passengers, employees and partners. The Board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations," Roald added.

    The company has canceled all flights, and ticket sales have been discontinued.

    Norse was founded in March 2021 and offered cheap flights between Europe, North America, Africa and Asia.

    According to recent reports, the Iran war began on Feb. 28 and caused jet fuel prices to skyrocket, forcing airlines around the world to grapple with higher costs. Prices are now up nearly 72% to $155 per barrel year-on-year as of the week ending Nov. 20, according to the International Air Transport Association's Jet Fuel Price Monitor.

    Norse Atlantic's Roald told CNBC in May that he wasn't "overly concerned" about access to fuel but flagged that the organization had canceled over 700 flights, which impacted more than 240,000 passengers.

    Ryanair's CEO Michael O'Leary warned in April that if jet fuel prices continued to stay elevated throughout the year, then other European airlines were likely to face "financial difficulties" during the winter season.

    In fact, several European airlines have stopped operating this winter, including Slovakia's AirExplore, Spain's AlbaStar, Ireland's Fly4 and Spain's Plus Ultra, which has canceled all flights but hasn't permanently closed.

    📅 15 Aug 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2508 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

    📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.
    • The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.
    • During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

    The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

    During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

    Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

    Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

    Sources indicate that jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

    Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

    After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

    It has been revealed that the North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

    It has been revealed that newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

    Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

    According to recent reports, referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

    A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

    Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

    Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

    There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

    Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

    It has been revealed that chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

    Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

    The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

    Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

    Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

    The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

    Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

    Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

    Industry observers note that play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

    Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

    Recent findings suggest that rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

    Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

    Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

    Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

    Recent findings suggest that newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

    Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

    According to recent reports, finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

    In a recent development, corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

    Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

    Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

    The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

    Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

    Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

    It has been revealed that newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

    Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

    Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

    Recent findings suggest that that was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

    Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

    According to recent reports, elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

    Sources indicate that the game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

    Industry observers note that bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

    Recent findings suggest that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

    According to recent reports, A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

    It has been revealed that leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

    Recent findings suggest that flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

    Industry observers note that newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

    Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

    Industry observers note that leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

    Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

    There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

    Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

    In a recent development, fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

    Newcastle get the game under way.

    Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

    The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

    Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

    Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

    Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

    Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

    It has been revealed that upcoming manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

    “It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

    Industry observers note that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

    Recent findings suggest that “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

    The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

    He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

    It has been revealed that “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

    “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

    Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

    It has been revealed that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he stated.

    “The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    The biggest money-making energy trade looks over. What to buy instead

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1789 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end?
    • Recent findings suggest that no, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV.
    • Recent findings suggest that I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What I'm hearing from energy insiders.

    Is one of the greatest money-making trades of the last few years coming to an end?

    Recent findings suggest that no, I'm not talking about Nvidia or any of the data center- or AI-related power companies (although they have been crushed lately too… more on that on CNBC TV. Tune in!).

    Recent findings suggest that I'm talking about whether the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding. Over the last year, the jump in some of these companies has been nothing short of remarkable.

    It has been revealed that that jump is largely due to massive increases in margins, earnings, and cash flow. Those have occurred because of a major jump in what is called a crack spread. That is the difference between the price of oil and the finished price of refined products such as diesel and jet fuel. For most of this year, spreads have been soaring as disruptions and attacks on facilities and shipping in the Arabian Gulf, Hormuz, and deep inside Russia have played havoc with the market. In the last week or so, however, something big has changed: many of those spreads have started to tighten.

    This seismic drop in spreads is causing a selloff in the aforementioned refinery companies.

    It has been revealed that if spreads continue to fall, these stocks may well keep selling off from recent highs. The upshot for investors may be that, as the shares come down, analysts see more upside. The median price target for Phillips 66 (PSX) now indicates a 20% gain from here, while smaller-cap Par Pacific (PARR) is double that.

    Here are a few other key points to focus on heading into the Thanksgiving-shortened week.

    In a recent development, I like to keep politics as much at arm's length as possible — we all know that energy and politics (sadly) often go hand in hand. Energy policies coming from Washington, D.C., can drive — or destroy — investment dollars. With all the major shifts in the White House over the last 10 years (four years of Trump, four years of Biden, and now 2 years into Trump #2), energy policies can blow through Washington faster than a summer squall hits a wind turbine. But because federal policies can mean so much for specific companies, sectors, and investments, it's key to follow the news flow.

    That noted, I'd like to take a moment to introduce you to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, known as BAAJA (and pronounced like the state in Mexico). Like much legislation, BAAJA is an obscure but key bill working its way through the American Congress. BAAJA does a lot of things, but what Power Insider readers care about is its focus on energy permitting reform. In a nutshell, BAAJA would help speed up the building of new electricity infrastructure. Again, that's an overly simplistic view of a massive bill, but it needs to be on your radar. The utility trade group Edison Electric Institute came out in favor of the legislation this month after the industry received some 11th-hour changes. See more about it in our recent interview with EEI President Drew Maloney here.

    According to recent reports, the bill passed the U.S. Senate in a vote late Thursday night. Now it moves to the House. Support for its final passage is also coming from the major LNG trade group, whose executive director said he "applauds the Senate for its bipartisan effort to pass meaningful, bipartisan, and durable permitting reforms aimed at delivering greater predictability, consistency, and certainty in the permitting, production, and export process for U.S. LNG. This legislation moves us closer to untangling red tape and eliminating overlapping agency reviews that can keep U.S. energy projects delayed for years.".

    According to recent reports, the Natural Gas Supply Association also chimed in, saying it urges Congress to see the bill as "a resource-agnostic and balanced reform agenda for boosting American energy security. It keeps strong environmental reviews in place, but it draws a firm line against the endless procedural delays that tie critical energy projects in knots for a decade.".

    In my view, passing BAAJA is an key test of Congress's appetite for helping the energy and electrical power industry, lowering costs, and speeding time to market. The old adage was correct: time is money. Literally. If BAAJA moves on through the House, we could see an upside move in some utility stocks and any company related to energy infrastructure.

    According to recent reports, speaking of politics, the news is getting lost in the massive Anthropic (ANT) IPO, but the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) — whose importance I wrote about in the last edition — just decided to resume permitting for data centers. The Texas Tribune did a nice write-up on it, and you can read it here.

    It's tough to say, but it's true. The two are inextricably linked by policies created at both the federal and state levels. As I wrote in the last edition, some federally elected officials may have less impact on state-level issues — like the data center buildout — but they certainly have power over national laws. While many of you are enthralled, disgusted, or confused by sordid tales of Nvidia and Jensen-gate, keep one eye open on what happens in Washington, D.C.

    Have a great week, and have a wonderful Thanksgiving, everyone.

    Perhaps the massive investor story — which is, like most things lately, related to Jensen-gate and Nvidia—is the sizable selloff in many AI, neocloud, and data center power-related stocks.

    Painful for current shareholders, but significant drops can also bring big opportunities. Wall Street believes that's the case, at least right now. Look at some of the potential upside based on the stocks' prices versus their price targets.

    Industry observers note that we spoke with the CEO of Applied Digital (APLD) about all of this on CNBC last week, and you can watch it here. He highlighted how the market may be getting these stock stories wrong because, at least with his organization, he has long-term contracts with solid-credit companies. In that way, Applied Digital is more like a landlord than a "pure-play" AI company.

    My take → While I'm not going to recommend a specific stock, I would add that it is critical for investors to understand the differences between these companies. While they may have some things in common, they are also different, with different business models, customers, leases, and sources of revenue.

    Speaking of recommendations… here are two ideas for you:.

    A recent decline presents a nice opportunity in SOLV Energy (MWH). UBS analyst Jon Windham upgrades SOLV to buy from neutral, believing the market is "underappreciating several key tailwinds for SOLV given uncertainty around data center demand and higher interest rates." UBS highlights how the stock has fallen lately despite making two deals and beating and raising recent guidance. UBS notes now is an "attractive entry point" for SOLV. (Side note: MWH is a great stock ticker.).

    While markets overall fall, BMO remains bullish on Bloom Energy (BE). After speaking with the company, the analyst is upgrading Bloom to outperform, saying he remains "increasingly confident of BE's commercial traction" and that he still has conviction even with the recent drop in shares. While analyst Ameet Thakkar did cut his target to $230 from $260, that's still 50% upside from the current price. Bloom shares have tumbled 45% since October 1.

    Industry observers note that I was recently asked for my opinion on the price of oil. Here's my take. The market clearly wants to push oil contract prices lower and has for a few months. But, as I've noted and reported for a while, don't confuse the futures (paper) price with the actual price. Yes, shipping rates and insurance rates have come down from recent highs — and there is a good amount of oil now flowing through Hormuz — but the cost of a physical barrel of crude is still well above the futures contract. If we get real, longer-lasting peace around Iran, oil prices will fall. There is plenty of oil in the world. That said, if bombs and missiles start firing again, oil prices will firm. I know that's a non-answer answer, but the oil market is truly headline-driven right now. My late good friend Boone Pickens (later in life, he didn't like being called by the "T" in his first name) used to avoid giving a set price target and instead give a directional quote, so I'll do the same: the odds of oil being lower in two months than it is today are 75%.

    According to recent reports, last week, I had a one-on-one with Vimal Kapur, chair and CEO of Honeywell International (HON), at an RBC conference in Newly introduced York City. While the conversation wasn't filmed, I can tell you that Kapur offered investors reassurance that his order book is doing very, very well. This is key because Honeywell is huge in the things that make other things work. Its sensors go into a ton of energy facilities, from refineries to LNG facilities. Honeywell is a leading indicator of spending and buildouts, so if it keeps getting orders, it's a good sign for macro energy.

    Bottom line: Watch Honeywell stock as a potential "tell.".

    According to recent reports, this week's Inside Line interview takes a different approach. We hit our friend Craig Johnson up for actionable insights into energy and stocks. Craig is managing director and chief market technician at Piper Sandler. He recently appeared on Power Lunch to talk about markets and stocks. He mentioned being bullish on energy, so we wanted to dig in just a little bit more.

    Recent findings suggest that this week, we had the pleasure of chatting with Balaji Krishnamurthy, president of Chevron Australia. We spoke at length about natural gas, the impact of disruptions, and long-term demand from Chevron customers in the Asia-Pacific region.

    This is a bit of a local RBI for the Newly introduced York City area, but one I felt was important to highlight. New York's electric grid operator just came out with a massive warning for everyone in our region: in just a couple of years, there may not be enough electricity supply to power our needs. A new report reveals a deficit in seven years, with a nearly 2 GW power hole in a decade. That's a number of substantial power plants' worth of energy. Get your solar panels on and buy that backup generator! I'll call this one random, but scary.

    Catch up with more on energy including interviews and video content from CNBC and Power Insider.

    Read the last concern of Power Insider here.

    #153819. AI shopping agents are having a moment, but Amazon and a growing number of sites threaten to stunt their growth

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1554 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech 📈 Bullish 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    AI shopping agents are having a moment, but Amazon and a growing number of sites threaten to stunt their growth

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that maia Bittner urgently needed to replace her car's windshield wipers.
    • Bittner, chief product officer at fintech startup Imprint, gave Muse the greenlight to buy some wipers on her behalf from AutoZone.
    • About 17 hours later, she got a notification from her Muse agent, saying AutoZone canceled her order due to an unspecified error.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that maia Bittner urgently needed to replace her car's windshield wipers. So last month, she turned to Meta's Muse personal artificial intelligence agent.

    Bittner, chief product officer at fintech startup Imprint, gave Muse the greenlight to buy some wipers on her behalf from AutoZone. Or so she thought.

    About 17 hours later, she got a notification from her Muse agent, saying AutoZone canceled her order due to an unspecified error.

    "Honestly, the most reliable path now is you ordering on Amazon yourself," Muse said, according to a screenshot of the message.

    The interaction encapsulates the current messy and complicated landscape of agentic shopping apps, the AI tools that can make purchases on behalf of customers. Over the past year, tech companies such as OpenAI, Meta, Google and Instinct have introduced versions of personal agents that promise to take the hassle out of browsing and buying online.

    The rollout has been far from smooth.

    While some major retailers, such as Walmart and Sephora, have opened up their sites to agents, companies including Amazon, eBay, United Airlines and Kohl's limit what actions agents can take or block them outright. Others have added provisions to their terms of service spelling out that they're not liable if users' AI-driven purchases go wrong.

    "It's a very mixed bag," Emily Pfeiffer, a principal analyst at Forrester, mentioned in an interview. "It means that a consumer who's using an agent to shop and browse and learn is not going to see the full set of options because some websites are unavailable.".

    The hiccups threaten to stunt the growth of shopping agents by creating a clunky and frustrating experience for consumers who are just starting to experiment with the tools. The question of who takes the blame when a transaction goes wrong also remains unclear.

    It has been revealed that despite those challenges, analysts remain bullish about agentic commerce's potential. U.S. revenue from agentic commerce could reach up to $1 trillion by 2030, analysts at McKinsey and ICSC forecast in April.

    Retailers and tech companies are also positioning agents as a helping hand for holiday shopping. Walmart on Tuesday touted its partnership with Meta, saying consumers could "put an AI agent to work" to nab Black Friday deals.

    Earlier this month, Shopify President Harley Finkelstein predicted this year would be the "first holiday season" where AI-driven shopping goes mainstream.

    "I think last year we saw AI influence more in discovery," Finkelstein told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." "I think now we're going to see more of that conversion.".

    For users hoping to turn their online shopping over to AI agents, the experience can be unpredictable.

    It has been revealed that agents encounter a patchwork of permissions across various websites. Retailers such as Coach and Gap allow AI bots to browse but not check out, while others such as Target sometimes "block shopping agents by accident," according to an audit conducted in August by agent security company Billions Network.

    In a recent development, amazon has responded the most aggressively to agents by walling off its site entirely. The tech giant rankled Elon Musk last month after it prevented his Grok Bot from placing orders.

    According to recent reports, in September, the tech giant also blocked Meta's Muse from shopping on its platform, saying it never agreed to participate in the program. And last November, Amazon sued Perplexity, accusing the startup of concealing its Comet agent, which can purchase products on behalf of people.

    Amazon CEO Andy Jassy has said the company expects "over time, to partner with third-party agents," but that any partnerships will require the right "value exchange" between agents and retailers.

    Bots encounter complications even when retailers welcome them in. They often fumble through webpages and get stumped by login requirements at checkout. In some cases, the agents may require human intervention to bypass a Captcha test and continue browsing.

    A Visa study published earlier this month instructed 22 models from 12 AI labs to carry out a range of shopping tasks, such as buying a TV, a laptop and a hair appliance. The agents failed about 43% of test runs, and in more than half of those failed runs, an agent purchased a product "that did not meet the customer's identified requirements," according to the study.

    In a recent development, bittner said she is a "big believer" in AI agents' potential. Earlier this year, she said, she was delighted when Perplexity's shopping agent found and purchased a pair of Adidas sneakers that were sold out for months.

    Industry observers note that other experiences have been clumsier. Last week, she stated, she asked Meta's Muse to help her find a Jellycat octopus plushie for her kids. It suggested a product marked 75% off from "Crazy Hobby Supply," a retailer she'd never heard of and that didn't appear to have any reviews, she said.

    Recent findings suggest that "I sort of trust Google to only surface sites that are not scams to me in their sponsored ads," Bittner noted. "In the same way, I want AI to only surface to me websites that are not scams. I don't think we're there yet.".

    Users have reported mishaps with other AI tools, including one case where Instinct's text-based agent booked a hotel and signed up for a loyalty program without the consumer's consent.

    Industry observers note that many retailers are approaching agents cautiously because they're concerned about fraudulent bot activity. San Francisco-based Skyfire is trying to solve that problem by arming retailers with more data to identify which bots are visiting their site and to verify that a human has actually consented to let an agent buy a product on their behalf.

    Typically, when a human visits a website, there are "all kinds of signals" to prove it's not a fraudulent user, Skyfire CEO Amir Sarhangi noted in an interview.

    Sources indicate that none of those things are available to retailers when an agent accesses their site, Sarhangi said. Agents might appear even more suspicious because they mask their IP address or origin via data centers, and they often use one-time, virtual cards to check out.

    Industry observers note that "So we talked to a lot of merchants and banks and financial institutions, and the things they told us were: We want to know who the end user is, and we want to know it's a real human," Sarhangi said. "We want to know who these agents are, because we're not going to just let willy-nilly anybody do these types of transactions, and we need a way to kind of verify that.".

    AI companies, retailers, financial institutions and other industries have announced an alphabet soup of "protocols," rules that propose ways to make it easier for agents to transact on websites.

    There's yet to be a broad consensus around who takes responsibility when an agent purchase goes sideways. American Express in April mentioned it would protect eligible customers "from charges related to AI agent error." Stripe, whose Link digital wallet is integrated with Muse, protects some agent purchases and offers a "refund guarantee.".

    Industry observers note that others are more wary. Last month, JPMorgan Chase blocked external agents from operating on behalf of customers, citing security concerns. Best Buy is among several retailers that deem users responsible for agent purchases in their terms of service. Best Buy says it views those transactions "as if you performed them yourself.".

    "Best Buy is not responsible for conduct, errors, actions, or inaction by any Digital Agent," the organization's terms say.

    Sarhangi remarked he can see why retailers, especially Amazon, are shutting their doors to external agents when the user experience remains inconsistent.

    "At the scale [Amazon] operates in, I would think they need it to be much more aligned with their existing processes, so that they're not going to have a bunch of unhappy owners saying, 'What's going on here?'" he remarked.

    It has been revealed that for now, agents remain a niche tool for shopping, with agentic purchases making up just 0.4% of global e-commerce transactions and 0.2% of value, according to Bain & Co. research published earlier this month.

    Uber disclosed last month that AI agents booked only 504 rides and Uber Eats orders during its busiest week in October. Airbnb also said it has seen little volume from agents, while DoorDash said it has recorded only "several hundred" agent orders so far.

    Recent findings suggest that but retailers may not be able to ignore them forever. Roughly a quarter of Muse's 10 million users are shopping online via an AI agent with an average spend of $200 per order, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in October.

    Instinct CEO Noah Shinn told CNBC earlier this month that the average transaction value among its consumers exceeds $500 per person.

    Asked about some companies' efforts to block agents, Shinn said he tries to "give them some slack.".

    "It's a latest interface, it's a new mode of where users' attention is coming from, and it might just disrupt existing large services of theirs," Shinn mentioned at a CNBC CEO Council dinner in San Francisco. "They just need time, and we've just done a lot of thinking on our side.".

    Sources indicate that "We can obviously move very fast and certain businesses cannot," he said. "So, how can we collaborate with them?".

    #153818. Carson Beck ruled out for Week 12, Josh Johnson to start

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1m • ⚡ Quick Read (15 w)

    #153814. The S&P 500 is in a correction. Bear markets and recessions don't always follow

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    The S&P 500 is in a correction. Bear markets and recessions don't always follow

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The S&P 500 fell into a correction on Nov.
    • Sources indicate that the market correction, defined as a 10% decline from a recent high, came as investor concern mounted over a potential slowdown in AI spending, mega-cap tech valuations and the path of Federal Reserve interest rate policy.
    • In a recent development, A correction can deepen into a bear market, defined as a drop of 20% or more from the most recent top.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The S&P 500 fell into a correction on Nov. 20 for the first time since April 2025 as stocks pulled back sharply from October's record highs.

    Sources indicate that the market correction, defined as a 10% decline from a recent high, came as investor concern mounted over a potential slowdown in AI spending, mega-cap tech valuations and the path of Federal Reserve interest rate policy. The S&P 500 fell 3.7% on Nov. 20 alone, closing at 6,910.39, its seventh consecutive daily decline. That left the index 11.6% below the Oct. 6 closing high of 7,818.93.

    In a recent development, A correction can deepen into a bear market, defined as a drop of 20% or more from the most recent top. But history shows that even a bear market, let alone a correction, doesn't automatically mean the economy is destined for a recession.

    In a CNBC analysis, eight of the 13 S&P 500 bear markets overlapped with recessions, as defined by the National Bureau of Economic Research, and five did not. The NBER states a recession is "a significant decline in economic activity that is spread across the economy and lasts more than a few months.".

    The 1973-74 oil shock, the dot-com bust in 2000, the 2007-09 financial crisis and the 2020 pandemic downturn all overlapped with recessions. But some major bear markets also occurred without one, including in 1987 and 2022.

    Sources indicate that deutsche Bank macro strategist Henry Allen said that every S&P 500 bear market since the 1962 "Kennedy Slide" has coincided with at least one of three factors: a recession, worsening economic data raising recession fears, or a cycle of Federal Reserve rate hikes. None of those are present today, at least so far.

    "Much as last week's selloff was severe, it's worth remembering that it has several differences with many of the other major risk-off moves in recent times," the London-based strategist wrote on Tuesday.

    Sources indicate that allen said there hasn't been any sudden reassessment of the growth outlook recently, which happened during the Covid-19 shock, when the pandemic pushed the global economy into recession and the S&P 500 plunged 33.9% in just 33 days. Nor is the current situation similar to the 2025 "Liberation Day" tariff period either, which also prompted a reassessment of the growth outlook.

    Economic numbers aren't deteriorating either, with the November U.S. flash composite Purchasing Managers' Index, or PMI, at 54.6, above 50 and indicating that business activity continued to expand. Another factor that often coincides with a recession, Allen said, was a big hawkish shift from the central banks, seen in the 1966 and 2022 bear markets.

    "Today however, the equity declines have not coincided with a hawkish repricing," despite widespread expectations that the central bank is set to raise rates again at its final meeting of the year, on Dec. 9, Allen remarked.

    Today, markets are pricing fewer Fed rate hikes through September 2027 than they were on Oct. 6, when the S&P 500 set its record, Allen mentioned. "If anything, pricing has shifted slightly dovishly with the equity declines.".

    Over more than six decades since 1962, bear markets have always coincided with at least one of those three circumstances, according to Allen.

    "So it would be unusual to see one today without those" happening too, he noted.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated.".
    • Data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S.
    • According to recent reports, that revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post, suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump on Thursday falsely deemed the latest gross domestic product revision a mistake, claiming that it should be "immediately investigated.".

    Data released Wednesday from the Commerce Department revealed that the U.S. economy exhibited much stronger growth for the third quarter than initially estimated, showing that real GDP grew at a 4.3% annualized rate. That was revised upward from the department's advance estimate of 3.4%.

    According to recent reports, that revision was a "RECORD SETTING ERROR," Trump said in a Truth Social post, suggesting that the initial release could have influenced the outcome of the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, where Democrats flipped both chambers of Congress and multiple governorships.

    "I would like to wish a Happy Thanksgiving to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%, A RECORD SETTING ERROR, and one so grave that it should be immediately investigated," Trump wrote.

    It has been revealed that however, the difference between the advance estimate and the figure in the second release is far from being an all-time record. It was the largest revision since the 1.2 percentage point revision seen in the second quarter of 2020.

    Recent findings suggest that on an absolute basis, the latest revision was tied for 16th among all revisions from the advance estimate to the second release since 1990. It also tied four other quarters with a similar 0.9 percentage point difference — and was approximately double the average revision of 0.43 percentage points for all 147 quarters.

    The upward revision highlights Trump's policies are "delivering results" that defy expectations, White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told CNBC.

    Revisions to U.S. economic numbers are not out of the ordinary. Initial reports count on partial survey data and early estimates. That data is later updated with more survey responses — which sometimes leads to changes from the initial reports.

    In a recent development, GDP data is revised repeatedly over a five-year period. By the time the final revision is done, the average absolute error from the second release to the final is 1.14 percentage points.

    Recent findings suggest that the advance estimate for Q3 U.S. GDP, which came just days before Election Day in early November, was still better than the figure economists had expected at the time. It also highlighted a significant step-up in growth from the second quarter.

    Because that was a strong showing for the economy, some on Wall Street consider this week's revision to be a confirmation of the economy's recent growth trend.

    Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors said immediately following the release that it "reinforces an increasingly familiar tension" that the economy is "performing quite well, but its resilience also gives the Fed an even stronger case for further rate hikes.".

    Industry observers note that "The economy isn't merely hanging in there. It continues to demonstrate considerable resilience, with consumers spending, businesses investing and few signs that restrictive monetary policy is creating significant cracks in the broader expansion," the firm's chief investment officer mentioned.

    In a recent development, traders are currently pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a hike at the Federal Open Market Committee's December meeting, according to the CME FedWatch tool. They're also anticipating an additional hike in January.

    — CNBC's Jeff Cox and Fred Imbert contributed reporting.

    • Investors and traders mentioned that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.
    • "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you blink, you may have missed it.

    Nvidia shares gapped higher at the open by more than 30%, on pace for its biggest one-day gain in 23 years on Monday, following the news just before the bell that former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is going to be reinstated.

    Investors and traders mentioned that while this reflex rally may have more to run, cautiousness is warranted on Nvidia and the AI trade because of the overhang of investigations into the alleged Chinese espionage involving the company and others, as well as the possibility for data center moratoriums as Democrats take control of Congress and key governor posts in January.

    "Am I as bullish on Nvidia now as I was on Friday? Of course not, you can't be," mentioned Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, which counted Nvidia as its largest position as he bought on the dip over the last few weeks. "I'm trimming back.".

    "All the same concerns that were here before Jensen resigned are still here," he added.

    Industry observers note that the day before Huang resigned on Nov. 12 as CEO, Nvidia closed at $173.73. It's intraday high on Monday was $171.50, up from its recent low around $125 as it was selling off in the wake controversies. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF closed at $506.96 the day before his resignation. It reached a high of $469.35 before losing steam as trading wore on Monday.

    Recent findings suggest that mike Khouw, YieldMax strategist at Tidal Financial Group, told CNBC on Monday that there were "sighs of relief," "applause" and even "cheering" among investors at the news of Huang's potential reinstatement. But he also said there are still considerable risks facing the AI trade.

    Sources indicate that jensen Huang was not the only problem at Nvidia, he stated, and there are still many vulnerabilities in the overall AI trade, which should give investors pause. Credit-sensitive companies are still at risk of faltering, Khouw added.

    Industry observers note that the national security implications of the scandal that has rocked Nvidia and the global AI trade more broadly aren't going away any time soon even as the Trump administration assured the Nvidia board there were none. Investors on Wall Street are expressing strategic concerns about ways to play the tech space just as lawmakers in Washington are demanding answers.

    Democrats are demanding answers on what exactly happened with Nvidia and the Chinese government.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) stated in a Monday statement. "The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement.".

    Sources indicate that house Ways and Means ranking member Richard Neal (D-Mass.) stressed the importance of Congressional oversight in determining the best course of action to move forward. The outcome of any Congressional investigations will likely be crucial for Nvidia's long-term viability as an investment opportunity, especially since the company does so much international business.

    "This is an export control issue," Neal told CNBC on Monday. "Congress is not subservient to this president or any other president as it relates to trade and tariff policies. This is a trade related issue.".

    Many of the same Democrats will call for a slowdown in the data center buildout, a strong glitch for the public partly responsible for their Blue Wave earlier this month.

    Recent findings suggest that "You're going to have to work your way through what these data center moratoriums all mean," said Niles. "Now I think the broader market keeps going but I am not as convinced on the move in the data-center centric names from here.".

    Recent findings suggest that to be sure, many Wall Street analysts were rushing to upgrade Nvidia's stock on Monday after Huang's reinstatement. Most restored price targets well above $200 with one as high as $270. But many traders think the rebound may fail before getting back to those levels.

    Famed short seller Michael Burry, who made a boatload betting against Nvidia with put options as it cratered, told his Substack audience that he thinks the rebound here could be "outsized," especially with low volume in the market overall because of the Thanksgiving holiday this week.

    But he too sees the rally eventually losing steam.

    "Jensen being back without much more information might even restore NVDA to the high 100s," Burry wrote. "I won't short it on this information I have today until it gets closer to or maybe hurdles $200.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.
    • Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.
    • His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

    Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

    His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

    Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

    Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

    United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

    United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

    Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

    But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

    Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

    AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

    Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

    That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand mentioned everything you need to know about this moment...

    Aug 22: Hull City vs Manchester United.

    Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town.

    Sep 6: Everton vs Manchester United.

    Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City.

    Sep 20: Fulham vs Manchester United.

    United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

    Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

    Four minutes of added time to be played...

    United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

    For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

    Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

    Industry observers note that more substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

    Major chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

    Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

    Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

    More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by upcoming signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

    Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

    Wholesale changes on the hour mark...

    Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

    For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

    In a recent development, milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

    Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

    United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

    Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

    Recent findings suggest that all square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

    Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

    Sources indicate that fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

    De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

    Recent findings suggest that manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

    The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

    According to recent reports, santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

    Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

    Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs.

    United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

    Recent findings suggest that shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

    Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

    United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

    A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

    Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

    A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

    Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

    Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

    In a recent development, amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

    Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

    Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

    Recent findings suggest that united make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

    Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

    The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

    Sources indicate that we are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

    Industry observers note that manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

    Industry observers note that marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

    Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

    The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the latest campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

    Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

    So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

    Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

    Aug 5: AC Milan 1 Inter Milan 1.

    In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE.

    Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha.

    Sources indicate that subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee.

    Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda.

    At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

    According to recent reports, “It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

    “I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

    “But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

    “Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”.

    New signing Youri Tielemans handed first start as one of six changes to the XI that faced Leeds United.
